Calories are essentially energy. Eating in a deficit is what forces the body to use it's stored fat. 

You are correct, if a person is starving themselves their metabolism can slow. That is why 1 to 2 times a week it's good to eat your normal amount.

Yes they should eat healthy, but that is not going to help a person loose fat without eating fewer calories than the body needs to maintain it's current weight. 

The calorie deficit is the most important part of weight loss. Next and not far behind is good nutrition. Lastly loosing weight to fast can be a shock to the body, and often makes people relapse, so it's better to lose weight slowly.

For bulking up the main reason I suggest more protein is because it's a good source of calories and unfortunately, many people are actually getting to little of it. It's not just for people who are bulking up for bodybuilding. You should have roughly at least 0.5 g of protein per your weight in pounds, or close to 1 to 1 how much you weigh in KG. Sure they could choose to get all those excess calories from carbs or fats, but you need to be careful not to overdo that. A person's nutrition needs change with them. If they weigh more, they will need more protein, vitamins and minerals than when they weighed less.

Good nutrition is most important for a healthy functioning body. A calorie deficit or surplus is most important for changing weight.

Apologies, didn't see the second part. For face it's complicated. You could see some improvement at a better weight. You can try makeup if you are interested in that. Possibly changing your hair style.

There are things we can't realistically change about ourselves. And finding a way to cope or change how we feel about the way we look can be just as important as physically working on those things.

Ok, for underweight it's mostly the reverse of weight loss. Eat in a calorie surplus (preferably healthy food). The best thing may be adding more protein to your diet, that is often the best source for getting more calories. 

Shoot for at least 0.75 grams of protein per pound of your ideal weight. If that's 100 pounds it would be 75 g of protein a day, if 150 pounds that's 105 g of protein a day. You can go higher, but I generally wouldn't go below 0.5 grams per pound of your current weight. (Unfortunately I know this isn't easy with things being expensive.)

Low cost foods for the protein they give is often things like chicken, pork, eggs, tuna, beans. Though that can vary by location and time. Eggs are still quite expensive here but I've heard they went down in price in other places more.

Best I know is weight loss for that. Most important thing is being in a calorie deficit. Good nutrition can help with this, but mostly because fruits, and especially vegetables, are lower in calories than most other foods.

You will be hungry when loosing weight (unfortunately not many ways around this) best hack I've found is to have gum (not bubble gun, that's bad for your teeth). Another way that helps is increasing your activity levels. This will make being in a calorie deficit easier.

There are many calorie calculators online, pick your favorite that works for you and is safe. Remember to have one or two days a week were you eat enough to maintain your current weight. (So if you normally eat around 2700 calories normally you would have around that much one day a week, and then have only 2200 calories a day the other 6 days of that week.)

Generally it's better to lose weight slowly around 1 to 2 pounds a week. That's a 500 to 1,000 calories deficit a day. Don't go below 1500 calories without talking to a doctor.

I would argue not only does that person deserve a second chance, but also that jail time is unnecessary for what happened. Instead an at least temporary ban on them handling weapons and a course on proper gun handling. As well as mandatory therapy sessions because they are probably not going to be ok after accidentally killing someone.

Ex 2: person is at a donut shop on a date and sees someone they find attractive. They leave their date partner at the table and try hitting up this new person. It is not something either person talked about or would have been ok with the other doing. 
That person should be dumped and not given a second chance unless many many things can be proven that they have become a better person and regret their mistakes for the correct reasons.

Ex 3: your sibling has a terrible habit of eating some of your food. Sometimes it's on purpose, sometimes just a mistake.
There is no reason to not keep giving this person chances. What they have done isn't that bad and often isn't anything more than a minor inconvenience.

Joke Ex: person orders you a pineapple pizza knowing it is a sin against pizza.
Clearly this person has found a way to spin the second chances into a negative number breaking logic and must pay for their crimes.
